newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM mulls sale of Northwest stake.
newsitem.headline: KLM mulls sale of Northwest stake.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines is mulling the sale of its 19 percent Northwest Airlines stake, Dutch daily De Telegraaf said on Wednesday.
A KLM spokesman was not immediately available for comment on the front page article, which said the Dutch airline was in talks with its U.S. partner to shed the stake.

Outgoing KLM president Pieter Bouw told a news conference in May the Dutch carrier was in talks with Northwest to resolve their boardroom battle over share ownership, adding he hoped to announce a positive outcome within the foreseeable future.
But he declined then to comment on speculation KLM was prepared to sell its Northwest stake in return for a multi-year partnership agreement.

De Telegraaf said on Wednesday that incoming KLM president Leo van Wijk, due to succeed Bouw on August 5, was seeking to shed KLM's stake in a last-ditch attempt to save the financially lucrative transatlantic alliance.
